These features are more typical of IDH-wildtype glioblastoma than lower-grade IDH-mutant astrocytoma. The absence of a T2-FLAIR mismatch also argues against the classic IDH-mutant astrocytoma imaging phenotype. Evidence against IDH-wildtype is that the lesion has cortical/temporal involvement and is solitary without satellites, which can be seen in IDH-mutant gliomas as well. Overall, the enhancing-necrotic high-grade pattern and age outweigh the less specific cortical-temporal location, so the best prediction is IDH-wildtype.

overall_comment: Predictions are based only on structural MRI metadata without diffusion, perfusion, spectroscopy, susceptibility/calcification assessment, or histology. The imaging phenotype is strongly high-grade and glioblastoma-like, but molecular confirmation is required, especially because adult diffuse glioma molecular subtype cannot be determined definitively from MRI metadata alone.
